title: Bury the dead
hook: Tobit risked his life to bury the dead
tomorrow: what did the stranger on the road do before he spoke?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: you came to me. The king asked whether you came, not what the prisoner did. Today, a dinner that ends at a grave.
screen: `YOU CAME TO ME.` → `A DINNER, THEN A GRAVE.`

segments.voice: Some family dinners take a turn. Someone mentions a will, or a plot at the cemetery, and the table goes quiet. The book of Tobit has a dinner like that. It's a feast day, and Tobit sends his son out to bring back one of their people to share the meal. The son comes back with news instead: one of them is lying dead in the street. Tobit leaves the table without eating. He carries the body home, hides it until the sun goes down, and buries it by night. He's done this before, and it nearly cost him his life.
screen: `A DINNER THAT TAKES A TURN.` → `A BODY IN THE STREET.` → `TOBIT LEAVES THE TABLE.`

segments.voice: Why leave a feast for that? In Tobit's world, a king had his people killed and left unburied. Burying them said: they still count. When the king found out, Tobit lost what he owned and fled. His neighbors mock him for starting again. Near the end of the book, the angel Raphael tells him that when he prayed with tears and buried the dead, Raphael offered his prayer to the Lord. The burials were part of the prayer. The Church names burying the dead among the corporal works of mercy, and asks that the bodies of the dead be treated with respect and charity, in hope of the resurrection. Now the question families face today, where Catholics land in two places. The Church permits cremation, as long as it isn't chosen to deny the resurrection. Some families choose it for cost, or for distance, or a family spread far apart, and it's allowed. The Church's own instruction still prefers burial: a body laid in the ground the way Jesus was laid in a tomb, sown in hope. And when there is cremation, it asks that the ashes rest in a sacred place, like a cemetery, rather than being scattered or kept at home, so the dead stay remembered and prayed for. The instruction's Latin name is worth repeating: Ad resurgendum cum Christo, to rise with Christ. Both sides of the table want what Tobit wanted with a shovel at night: this person mattered.
screen: `BURYING THEM SAID: THEY COUNT.` · `THE BURIALS WERE PART OF THE PRAYER.` · `CREMATION ALLOWED, BURIAL PREFERRED.` · `ASHES REST IN A SACRED PLACE.` · then, large: `HONOR THE DEAD.`

segments.voice: Find a photo of someone who has died, on your phone or on a shelf, or just write their name down. Look at it for the whole sit, without hurrying past. If you pray, you can pray for them the way Catholics pray at a graveside; if not, simply let them be remembered.
Bury the dead. Lay the dead to rest with honor, and keep them remembered, the way Tobit did in the dark.
Your line: honor the dead. Both sides of that dinner table want the same thing. Rest well.
